choices: Schema discovery in the schema registry
Resource-based policies on the event bus
Scheduled rules that use a cron expression
explanation: EventBridge can archive the events sent to an event bus, for a set period or indefinitely, and later replay them from the archive, so a team can re-run recent events after fixing a consumer.

choiceExplanations.0: The schema registry stores the structure of events so developers can write code against them; it does not keep copies of the events to send again.
choiceExplanations.2: A resource-based policy controls which other AWS accounts may send events to the bus; it does not store or resend events.
choiceExplanations.3: A scheduled rule invokes a target on a time schedule; it does not re-deliver events that have already passed through the bus.

resources.title: Archiving and replaying events in Amazon EventBridge

question:
An analyst has years of log files stored as CSV and Parquet in Amazon S3. She wants to run ad hoc SQL queries on them without provisioning servers or loading the data anywhere else, and to pay only for the queries she runs.
Which service should she use?
choices: Amazon Athena, querying the files in place
explanation: Athena is a serverless service that runs standard SQL directly on files in Amazon S3, such as CSV and Parquet, with no servers to manage and pricing based on the data each query scans.

choiceExplanations.0: A provisioned Redshift cluster must be sized and paid for while it runs, and data is normally loaded into it first, which goes against the no-servers, no-loading requirement.
choiceExplanations.1: EMR runs clusters of instances that you launch and configure, so it is not serverless and takes more setup than an ad hoc SQL query needs.
choiceExplanations.2: QuickSight builds dashboards and reports; it is a visualization service, not the serverless SQL query engine the analyst asked for.

question:
A retail company wants a data warehouse where analysts can run complex SQL aggregations over petabytes of historical sales data and connect their BI tools. The work is analytics, not transaction processing.
Which AWS service is the best fit?
explanation: Redshift is a managed data warehouse built for analytics (OLAP): columnar storage and a parallel query engine run complex SQL over petabytes of data, and BI tools connect to it.

choiceExplanations.1: RDS for MySQL is a row-based relational database aimed at transactional (OLTP) workloads, and it is not built for petabyte-scale analytical queries.
choiceExplanations.2: DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value and document database for low-latency lookups; it is not a SQL data warehouse for complex aggregations.
choiceExplanations.3: ElastiCache is an in-memory cache that speeds up reads for an existing database; it does not store petabytes of historical data for analysis.

question:
A company has 12 AWS accounts that are each billed separately. Finance wants a single bill for all of them, and wants the combined usage to qualify for volume pricing discounts.
Which service should the company use?
choices: AWS Cost Explorer with saved reports
AWS IAM Identity Center permission sets
explanation: AWS Organizations groups accounts under one management account. Consolidated billing gives one payment method and one bill, and combines usage across accounts so it can reach volume pricing tiers and share Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts.

choiceExplanations.0: Cost Explorer analyzes and visualizes costs and usage; it does not merge several accounts into one bill or change what the accounts are charged.
choiceExplanations.1: Cost Anomaly Detection alerts you to unusual spending; it does not combine bills or add up usage across accounts.
choiceExplanations.3: IAM Identity Center manages workforce sign-in and permissions across accounts and has no effect on how the accounts are billed.

resources.title: Effective billing date, account activity, and volume discounts

question:
A finance team wants to see how much each AWS service has cost per month over the past year and get a forecast of future usage, using built-in charts and reports.
Which AWS tool should the team use?
explanation: Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes AWS costs and usage over time, can group them by service, and forecasts future usage, with built-in charts and custom reports.

choiceExplanations.1: CloudTrail records API activity for auditing, so it shows who did what, not how much each service costs.
choiceExplanations.2: Config records resource configurations and how they change over time; it does not report spending or forecast usage.
choiceExplanations.3: CloudWatch Logs Insights queries log data from applications and services; it holds no billing breakdown or forecast.

resources.title: Exploring your data using Cost Explorer

question: Which AWS service sets up and governs a secure, compliant multi-account environment using best practices and guardrails?
explanation: AWS Control Tower is the easy way to set up and govern a secure, compliant multi-account AWS environment: it builds on AWS Organizations, automates the setup in a few clicks, and applies ongoing guardrails.

choiceExplanations.0: CloudTrail records the API calls made in an account; it does not set up accounts or apply governance guardrails across them.
choiceExplanations.2: Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure; it does not set up or govern a multi-account environment.
choiceExplanations.3: KMS creates and manages encryption keys; it does not build or govern a multi-account environment.

question: Which AWS service provisions and automatically renews the TLS certificates used for HTTPS on a load balancer?
explanation: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provisions and manages TLS certificates, renews them automatically, and deploys them to integrated services such as Elastic Load Balancing.

choiceExplanations.0: KMS creates and manages the encryption keys that protect stored data; it does not issue or renew TLS certificates for HTTPS.
choiceExplanations.1: Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets such as database credentials and API keys; it does not provision TLS certificates for a load balancer.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS WAF filters web requests with rules, for example to block SQL injection; it does not issue or renew certificates.

question: Which AWS service records how resource configurations change over time and checks them against compliance rules?
explanation: AWS Config records the configuration of your resources and how it changes over time, and evaluates it against rules so you can see whether resources are compliant.

choiceExplanations.0: Inspector scans EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and network exposure; it does not keep a configuration history.
choiceExplanations.1: Shield protects applications from DDoS attacks; it does not record resource configurations or evaluate compliance.
choiceExplanations.3: Firewall Manager applies firewall and security policies centrally across accounts in an organization; it does not record how resources change over time.

question: Which AWS service automatically adds EC2 instances when load rises and removes them when it falls?
explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling keeps a group of instances between a minimum and a maximum size, adding instances when load rises (scale out) and removing them when it falls (scale in).

choiceExplanations.1: Elastic Load Balancing spreads incoming traffic across the instances you already have; it does not launch or terminate instances.
choiceExplanations.2: Route 53 answers DNS queries and routes users to endpoints; it does not add or remove EC2 instances.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Backup creates and manages backups of your data; it has nothing to do with the number of running instances.

resources.title: What is Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling?

question: Which AWS service centrally manages and automates backups across services such as Amazon EBS, Amazon RDS and Amazon EFS?
explanation: AWS Backup is a fully managed service that centrally configures and automates backups across many AWS services, so you do not need custom scripts for each one.

choiceExplanations.0: Snowball is a physical device for moving large amounts of data into or out of AWS; it does not schedule or manage backups.
choiceExplanations.2: CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs and raises alarms; it does not back up data.
choiceExplanations.3: DataSync copies data between storage systems and AWS storage services; it does not provide a central policy for backing up many services.

question: Which TWO types of target can an Application Load Balancer send requests to? (Choose TWO.)
explanation: An Application Load Balancer routes requests to the targets in its target groups, and those targets can be EC2 instances, IP addresses and Lambda functions.

choiceExplanations.1: S3 buckets cannot be registered in a target group; static content from S3 is normally served through CloudFront.
choiceExplanations.3: DynamoDB tables are databases that applications call through an API; they are not registered as load balancer targets.
choiceExplanations.4: SQS queues hold messages for consumers to poll; they are not registered as load balancer targets.

resources.title: Target groups for your Application Load Balancers

question: Which AWS service provides a managed file system that many Linux EC2 instances can mount at the same time?
explanation: Amazon EFS is a managed network file system (NFS) that many Linux EC2 instances, even in different Availability Zones, can mount at the same time. It grows and shrinks automatically.

choiceExplanations.0: EBS is block storage that is normally attached to a single instance, not a shared file system for many instances.
choiceExplanations.1: S3 Glacier is archival object storage for rarely accessed data; it cannot be mounted as a file system by instances.
choiceExplanations.3: Instance store is temporary storage physically attached to one host, and its data is lost when the instance stops, so it cannot be shared.

question: Which fully managed, serverless AWS service extracts, transforms and loads data to prepare it for analytics?
explanation: AWS Glue is a serverless data integration service that runs extract, transform and load (ETL) jobs to prepare and move data, for example from S3 into a data warehouse.

choiceExplanations.0: QuickSight builds dashboards and visualizations from data that is already prepared; it is not an ETL service.
choiceExplanations.1: Athena runs SQL queries on data in S3; it analyzes data in place rather than extracting, transforming and loading it.
choiceExplanations.2: OpenSearch Service is a search and log analytics engine; it is not a service for running ETL jobs.

question: Which EC2 purchasing option gives the deepest discount for workloads that can handle interruptions?
explanation: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at discounts of up to 90% compared with On-Demand, but AWS can reclaim them, so they suit workloads that tolerate interruption.

choiceExplanations.1: On-Demand Instances are billed at the full hourly rate with no commitment, so they cost more than Spot.
choiceExplanations.2: Reserved Instances give a discount in return for a one- or three-year commitment, but the discount is smaller than Spot's and they are meant for steady, always-on use.
choiceExplanations.3: Dedicated Hosts give you a whole physical server, usually for licensing or compliance needs, and are one of the more expensive options.

question: Which AWS service uses machine learning to detect unusual spending and alert you to it?
explanation: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection monitors your cost and usage with machine learning, learns your normal spending pattern, and alerts you to unusual spikes without you defining thresholds.

choiceExplanations.0: CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs and can alarm on thresholds you set; it does not use machine learning to spot unusual spending patterns on its own.
choiceExplanations.1: Organizations groups accounts and provides consolidated billing; it does not analyze spending for unusual patterns.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Backup creates and manages backups of your data; it does not monitor or analyze spending.

resources.title: Detecting unusual spend with AWS Cost Anomaly Detection

question: What does AWS KMS do?
choices: Records every API call in an account
explanation: AWS KMS (Key Management Service) creates and manages the encryption keys that protect your data, and it is integrated with most AWS services such as EBS, S3 and RDS.

choiceExplanations.1: Recording API calls is what AWS CloudTrail does; KMS manages keys (although the use of KMS keys can be audited in CloudTrail).
choiceExplanations.2: Blocking common web exploits such as SQL injection is the job of AWS WAF, not KMS.
choiceExplanations.3: Issuing and renewing TLS certificates is done by AWS Certificate Manager; KMS manages encryption keys.

question: When would you use AWS Secrets Manager?
choices: To record API calls in an account
To store and rotate database credentials
explanation: Secrets Manager stores secrets such as database credentials and API keys, encrypts them with KMS, and can rotate them automatically on a schedule, so credentials do not sit in your code.

choiceExplanations.0: Blocking SQL injection is the job of AWS WAF; Secrets Manager does not inspect web requests.
choiceExplanations.1: Scanning workloads for software vulnerabilities is what Amazon Inspector does; Secrets Manager stores secrets.
choiceExplanations.2: Recording API calls in an account is what AWS CloudTrail does; Secrets Manager stores secrets.

question: What does AWS Network Firewall do?
choices: Filters network traffic for a VPC
explanation: AWS Network Firewall is a managed firewall that protects an entire VPC: it inspects traffic in any direction, from layer 3 to layer 7, and can allow, drop or alert on traffic that matches your rules.

choiceExplanations.0: Scanning instances for software vulnerabilities is what Amazon Inspector does.
choiceExplanations.1: Storing and rotating database secrets is what AWS Secrets Manager does.
choiceExplanations.3: Detecting threats by analyzing logs is what Amazon GuardDuty does; it raises findings rather than filtering traffic.

question: What does Amazon Route 53 do?
choices: Translates domain names to IP addresses
explanation: Route 53 is AWS's highly available DNS service: it translates domain names such as example.com into IP addresses, and it can also register domain names and route users to healthy endpoints.

choiceExplanations.0: Distributing traffic across instances is what Elastic Load Balancing does; Route 53 answers DNS queries.
choiceExplanations.2: Storing files as objects is what Amazon S3 does.
choiceExplanations.3: Queuing messages between services is what Amazon SQS does.

question: When would you use Amazon SQS?
choices: To decouple components with a queue
explanation: SQS is a fully managed message queue used to decouple the parts of an application: producers send messages to the queue, and consumers poll them at their own pace.

choiceExplanations.0: Translating domain names is what Route 53 does.
choiceExplanations.1: Encrypting data at rest is done with AWS KMS and the encryption options of each storage service; SQS queues messages.
choiceExplanations.3: Distributing traffic across instances is what Elastic Load Balancing does.

resources.title: What is Amazon Simple Queue Service?

question: Which TWO Amazon S3 features help protect objects from accidental deletion? (Choose TWO.)
explanation: S3 Versioning keeps every version of an object, so a deleted or overwritten object can be restored. MFA Delete requires an MFA code before an object version can be permanently deleted or versioning suspended.

choiceExplanations.1: Transfer Acceleration speeds up long-distance transfers through edge locations; it does not protect objects from deletion.
choiceExplanations.3: Requester Pays makes the requester pay the request and transfer costs; it does not protect objects from deletion.
choiceExplanations.4: Static website hosting serves a bucket's content as a website; it does not protect objects from deletion.

resources.title: Retaining multiple versions of objects with S3 Versioning

question: When would you use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server?
choices: To run SQL queries on S3 files
explanation: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed Windows file share: it supports the SMB protocol and Windows NTFS and integrates with Microsoft Active Directory, so Windows-based applications get shared file storage in AWS.

choiceExplanations.0: Queuing messages between services is what Amazon SQS does.
choiceExplanations.1: Caching data in memory is what Amazon ElastiCache does.
choiceExplanations.2: Running SQL queries on files in S3 is what Amazon Athena does.

resources.title: What is FSx for Windows File Server?

question: Which AWS service collects and stores streaming data in real time?
explanation: Kinesis Data Streams collects and stores streaming data in real time, such as clickstreams, IoT data and logs, so applications can process it as it arrives.

choiceExplanations.1: Athena runs SQL queries on data that is already stored in S3; it does not collect streaming data.
choiceExplanations.2: Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics; it is not the service that ingests and stores streaming records as they arrive.
choiceExplanations.3: QuickSight builds dashboards and visualizations; it does not collect streaming data.

resources.title: What is Amazon Kinesis Data Streams?

question: When are EC2 Reserved Instances a good fit?
choices: Short jobs that can be interrupted
Workloads that need a whole server
explanation: Reserved Instances give a significant discount compared with On-Demand in return for a one- or three-year commitment, so they fit steady-state workloads that run continuously, such as a database.

choiceExplanations.0: Short jobs that can be interrupted suit Spot Instances, which are cheaper but can be reclaimed by AWS.
choiceExplanations.2: One-off tests with unpredictable timing suit On-Demand Instances, which need no commitment.
choiceExplanations.3: Needing a whole physical server is the use case for Dedicated Hosts.

resources.title: Reserved Instances for Amazon EC2 overview

question: What does S3 Intelligent-Tiering do automatically?
choices: Moves objects between tiers by usage
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on how often they are used, saving money on data with changing or unknown access patterns, with no retrieval charges.

choiceExplanations.0: Replicating objects to another Region is done by S3 Replication, not by Intelligent-Tiering.
choiceExplanations.1: Deleting objects after a set time is done by an S3 Lifecycle expiration rule, not by Intelligent-Tiering.
choiceExplanations.3: Encrypting objects is a bucket or object setting (such as SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS); Intelligent-Tiering concerns access tiers.

question:
A company keeps its users in an on-premises Microsoft Active Directory. Employees must sign in to AWS-hosted applications with their existing credentials, and the company does not want to store directory data in AWS or run a second directory.
Which AWS Directory Service option should the company use?
choices: AD Connector, forwarding sign-in requests to the on-premises directory
AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a trust to the on-premises directory
Simple AD, joined to the on-premises directory
An Amazon Cognito user pool that imports the on-premises users
explanation: AD Connector is a directory gateway: it redirects authentication requests to the on-premises Active Directory, so users stay managed on premises and no second directory is created or cached in AWS.

choiceExplanations.1: AWS Managed Microsoft AD creates a separate directory in AWS that only trusts the on-premises one, so the company would run a second directory, which it wanted to avoid.
choiceExplanations.2: Simple AD is a standalone AD-compatible directory in AWS; it cannot be joined to an on-premises directory or take part in trust relationships.
choiceExplanations.3: A Cognito user pool is a separate user directory for application users; importing the users stores them in AWS and does not use the existing Active Directory sign-in.

question:
A company is publishing an edge-optimized Amazon API Gateway REST API in eu-west-1 under its own domain name, api.example.com. It wants HTTPS with a certificate from AWS Certificate Manager.
In which Region must the certificate be requested?
choices: eu-west-1, the same Region as the API
Each Region where its customers are located
us-east-1, because edge-optimized endpoints use CloudFront
Any Region, because ACM certificates are global
explanation: An edge-optimized endpoint is served through CloudFront, so the ACM certificate for its custom domain name must be requested in us-east-1, whichever Region the API itself runs in.

choiceExplanations.0: The same-Region rule applies to Regional endpoints; an edge-optimized API is fronted by CloudFront, so its certificate has to be in us-east-1.
choiceExplanations.1: A certificate is requested once, in a single Region; it is not created in each Region where customers are located.
choiceExplanations.3: ACM certificates are Regional resources, not global ones, and the Region matters: edge-optimized custom domains need the certificate in us-east-1.

resources.title: Set up an edge-optimized custom domain name in API Gateway
Get certificates ready in AWS Certificate Manager

question:
A financial company must keep its encryption keys in dedicated hardware that no other AWS customer shares. It wants to manage the keys itself so that AWS cannot use them.
Which service meets these requirements?
choices: AWS KMS with an AWS managed key, a multi-tenant service
AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation enabled
S3 server-side encryption with S3 managed keys (SSE-S3)
AWS CloudHSM, with the keys managed by the company itself
explanation: AWS CloudHSM provisions dedicated, single-tenant hardware security modules in your VPC, and you manage the keys entirely yourself, so AWS cannot use them.

choiceExplanations.0: KMS runs on a shared (multi-tenant) HSM model that AWS operates, and an AWS managed key is controlled by AWS, so it does not give dedicated hardware or key control.
choiceExplanations.1: Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets such as database credentials; it does not give you dedicated hardware for your own encryption keys.
choiceExplanations.2: With SSE-S3, AWS manages the keys and the encryption on your behalf, so the company neither controls the keys nor gets dedicated hardware.

question:
A company runs critical applications and databases on physical servers in its own data center. It wants a disaster recovery site in AWS that stays in sync within seconds, costs little while idle, and can fail over in minutes without redesigning the applications.
Which solution should it use?
choices: AWS Backup, copying nightly backups of the servers to another Region
AWS DMS, replicating the databases continuously to Amazon RDS
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery, with continuous block-level replication
AWS DataSync, copying server files to Amazon S3 on a schedule
explanation: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates entire servers at the block level into low-cost staging resources in AWS, so recovery points are seconds old and failover launches full servers in minutes, with failback afterwards.

choiceExplanations.0: Nightly backups mean hours of possible data loss and a slow restore, not seconds of lag and a failover in minutes.
choiceExplanations.1: DMS replicates databases only and targets a different database service, so it does not recover the applications and servers without redesign.
choiceExplanations.3: DataSync copies files on a schedule; it does not replicate whole servers or provide a fast failover.

question:
A data team stores very large objects in Amazon S3. Before downloading a 50 GB file, a script must read only the first few megabytes (the file header) to check its format, and the team also wants the full downloads to finish faster.
Which approach supports both needs?
choices: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket and download the whole file
Re-upload the objects with multipart upload so they can be read in parts
Copy each object to Amazon EFS first, then read the header from the copy
Use byte-range fetches, reading the header and downloading parts in parallel
explanation: Byte-range fetches use the HTTP Range header to request specific byte ranges of an object. The script can read just the header, and the team can download the file in parallel parts for a faster full download.

choiceExplanations.0: Transfer Acceleration speeds up long-distance transfers through edge locations, but the script would still have to download the whole file to see the header.
choiceExplanations.1: Multipart upload applies to uploading objects, not to reading them back, and it does not let a script read only the header.
choiceExplanations.2: Copying 50 GB objects to EFS first is slow and expensive and does nothing that S3 cannot already do by reading a byte range directly.

question:
A company runs Apache Kafka on premises. It wants to move to AWS, keep its existing Kafka producers and consumers, and stop managing broker and ZooKeeper servers.
Which TWO statements about Amazon MSK apply to this plan? (Choose TWO.)
choices: Producers and consumers must be rewritten to use the Kinesis API
MSK creates and manages the Kafka brokers and ZooKeeper nodes
The company must patch and replace failed broker servers itself
Existing Kafka applications can connect without code changes
Messages are kept only in memory and are lost when a broker restarts
explanation: Amazon MSK is fully managed Apache Kafka: it creates and manages the brokers and ZooKeeper nodes and recovers from common failures, and because it runs open-source Kafka, existing applications and tools work without code changes.

choiceExplanations.0: Rewriting for the Kinesis API is what moving to Kinesis Data Streams would require; MSK keeps the Kafka API, so no rewrite is needed.
choiceExplanations.2: Managing, patching and replacing broker servers is exactly the work MSK takes over, including automatic recovery from common Kafka failures.
choiceExplanations.4: MSK stores data on EBS volumes for as long as you choose, so messages are not lost when a broker restarts.

resources.title: Welcome to the Amazon MSK Developer Guide

question:
A company runs software that is licensed per physical socket and per core, and the license terms require it to see and report the physical servers used. It wants to reuse the licenses it already owns instead of buying new ones.
Which EC2 option is the most cost-effective choice?
choices: Default-tenancy On-Demand Instances on shared hardware
Dedicated Hosts, using the company's existing licenses
Spot Instances, to lower the hourly price
explanation: A Dedicated Host is a physical server dedicated to you, with visibility into its sockets and cores, so you can reuse existing per-socket or per-core licenses (bring your own license) instead of paying for new ones.

choiceExplanations.0: On-Demand Instances on shared hardware give no visibility into sockets or cores, so the license terms cannot be met.
choiceExplanations.2: Dedicated Instances keep your hardware separate from other customers but give no visibility into sockets and cores or control over placement, so they do not satisfy the license terms.
choiceExplanations.3: Spot Instances lower the hourly price but run on shared hardware that can be reclaimed, so they cannot meet the license reporting requirement.

question:
A reporting application in a company's data center queries a large database in AWS. Each query pulls about 100 MB of raw data to the data center, but the report it produces is only about 50 KB. The company's data transfer charges are high.
Which change reduces the transfer cost the most?
choices: Move the database to a larger instance type
Put a CloudFront distribution in front of the database
Run the reporting application in AWS beside the database
Replicate the database to a Region closer to the data center
explanation: Data transfer out of AWS is charged while transfer in is free, so running the application next to the database means only the 50 KB result leaves AWS instead of 100 MB of raw data per query.

choiceExplanations.0: A larger instance changes compute capacity, not how much data is sent out of AWS, so the transfer charges stay the same.
choiceExplanations.1: CloudFront caches and delivers web content over HTTP and HTTPS; it does not sit in front of a database connection, so the raw query data would still leave AWS.
choiceExplanations.3: Replicating to another Region adds inter-Region transfer charges and still sends the raw data out to the data center.

question:
A company shares an Amazon S3 bucket with every account in its AWS Organization. Accounts are added and removed every month, and the security team does not want to edit the bucket policy each time.
Which bucket policy approach meets this requirement?
choices: List every member account ID in the Principal element of the bucket policy
Allow all principals and add a condition on the organization ID with aws:PrincipalOrgID
Create an IAM user in each account and share its access keys with the bucket owner
Make the bucket public and restrict access with object ACLs
explanation: The aws:PrincipalOrgID condition key limits a resource-based policy to principals from accounts that belong to a specific AWS Organization, so accounts are covered automatically as they join or leave.

choiceExplanations.0: Listing account IDs works, but the policy must be edited every time an account joins or leaves, which is exactly what the team wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.2: Sharing access keys between accounts is insecure and does not scale, and it still needs manual changes for every new account.
choiceExplanations.3: A public bucket is open to everyone on the internet, not only to the organization's accounts.

resources.title: Examples of Amazon S3 bucket policies

question:
A company encrypts its EBS volumes with a KMS key in eu-west-2. For disaster recovery it must copy the volume snapshots to ap-southeast-2, and the copies must stay encrypted.
How should the company copy the snapshots?
choices: Copy the snapshot and rely on the source KMS key, which works in every Region
Ask AWS Support to replicate the source KMS key into the destination Region
Copy the snapshot unencrypted, because encrypted snapshots cannot leave their Region
Copy the snapshot and encrypt the copy with a KMS key in the destination Region
explanation: A regular KMS key stays in the Region where it was created. When an encrypted snapshot is copied to another Region, the copy is re-encrypted with a KMS key that exists in the destination Region.

choiceExplanations.0: A regular KMS key cannot be used in another Region, so the source key cannot encrypt or decrypt the copy there.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS Support does not replicate KMS keys between Regions; the copy is simply encrypted under a key in the destination Region.
choiceExplanations.2: Encrypted snapshots can be copied to other Regions and the copy can stay encrypted, so there is no reason to give up encryption.

question:
A company wants its team leads to create IAM roles for their applications without waiting for the security team, but no role they create may ever exceed a defined set of maximum permissions.
Which IAM feature should the company use?
explanation: A permissions boundary is a managed policy that sets the maximum permissions an IAM user or role can have. Team leads can be allowed to create roles only when they attach the boundary, so no role they create can exceed it.

choiceExplanations.1: SCPs set the maximum permissions for whole accounts or organizational units, not for the roles that one person creates.
choiceExplanations.2: An IAM group attaches policies to its users, but a group cannot act as a permissions boundary or cap the roles a user creates.
choiceExplanations.3: Resource-based policies are attached to resources such as S3 buckets to grant access to them; they do not limit the permissions of roles that users create.

question:
A web application behind an Application Load Balancer keeps each user's shopping cart in the memory of the EC2 instance that served them. The team enables duration-based sticky sessions on the target group.
Which TWO statements describe the effect? (Choose TWO.)
choices: The load balancer keeps a copy of each cart outside the instances
Requests from a client keep going to the same instance until the cookie expires
Health checks are no longer needed for the instances
Load can become unevenly spread across the instances
The stickiness cookie is created by the EC2 instance
explanation: With stickiness the load balancer sends a client's requests to the same instance until the stickiness cookie expires. That keeps in-memory sessions working, but it can leave some instances with more load than others.

choiceExplanations.0: Stickiness only routes a client to the same instance; the load balancer does not store session data, so the cart is still lost if that instance fails.
choiceExplanations.2: Health checks are still needed: the load balancer keeps checking the targets and stops routing to unhealthy ones.
choiceExplanations.4: With duration-based stickiness the load balancer generates the cookie (AWSALB); the EC2 instance does not create it.

resources.title: Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer

question:
A single EC2 instance serves a public application. When it fails, the team wants to bring up a standby instance quickly and keep clients using the same public IP address.
Which feature should the team use?
explanation: An Elastic IP address is a static public IPv4 address that you own until you release it. It can be quickly remapped from a failed instance to a standby instance, so clients keep using the same IP address.

choiceExplanations.0: An Auto Scaling group can replace a failed instance, but the replacement gets a new public IP address unless an Elastic IP is also remapped to it.
choiceExplanations.1: A weighted record changes which IP address DNS returns, so clients only switch after cached answers expire, and the public IP address does not stay the same.
choiceExplanations.3: An internet gateway connects the VPC to the internet; it does not keep a public IP address or move it between instances.

resources.title: Floating IP pattern for HA between active–standby stateful servers

question:
A database's data is stored on an EBS volume in us-east-1a. The team is replacing its instance with one in us-east-1b and must keep all of the data on the new instance's volume.
Which approach works?
choices: Detach the volume and attach it to the new instance in us-east-1b
Create a snapshot of the volume and create a new volume from it in us-east-1b
Turn on Multi-Attach for the volume and attach it to both instances
Change the volume's Availability Zone in the volume settings
explanation: An EBS volume lives in one Availability Zone and can be attached only to instances in that zone. To move the data, take a snapshot and create a new volume from it in the target zone.

choiceExplanations.0: A volume can be attached only to an instance in its own Availability Zone, so it cannot be attached to an instance in us-east-1b.
choiceExplanations.2: Multi-Attach lets several instances in the same Availability Zone use one volume; it does not let an instance in another zone attach it.
choiceExplanations.3: The Availability Zone of an existing volume cannot be changed; a new volume has to be created from a snapshot.

resources.title: Replace an Amazon EBS volume using a snapshot

question:
A memory-heavy application takes about ten minutes to start and warm its in-memory caches after every reboot. The team stops the EC2 instance at night to save money and wants the application back in its previous state quickly each morning.
Which option does this?
choices: Stop the instance at night and start it again in the morning
Create an AMI each night and launch a new instance from it in the morning
Move the application to an instance type with more memory
Hibernate the instance at night and start it again in the morning
explanation: EC2 Hibernate saves the contents of RAM to the encrypted root EBS volume before stopping. When the instance starts, it resumes with its in-memory state, so the application does not have to boot and warm up again.

choiceExplanations.0: A normal stop and start clears memory, so the operating system must boot and the application must warm up again.
choiceExplanations.1: An AMI captures disk contents, not the contents of memory, and launching from it still boots the operating system and restarts the application.
choiceExplanations.2: A larger instance does not keep memory contents across a stop and start, so the application would still need to warm its caches.

question:
An application reads product prices from an RDS database through an ElastiCache cache. Prices change a few times a day, and customers must never be shown a stale price after a change.
Which caching strategy should the team use?
explanation: Write-through updates the cache every time the database is written, so cached data is never stale. Lazy loading only fills the cache after a miss, so it can keep serving an old value until the entry expires.

choiceExplanations.0: A session store keeps temporary user session data (with TTLs) in the cache; it is not a way to keep cached database rows current.
choiceExplanations.2: Lazy loading caches data only when it is read, so after a price change the cache can keep returning the old price.
choiceExplanations.3: Read replicas spread read load across copies of the database, but they are not a cache and do not update the cache when a price changes.

question:
A company stores project files on an Amazon EFS Standard file system. Most files are not opened again after about two months, but they must stay on the file system, and storage costs keep growing.
Which change lowers the cost with the least effort?
choices: Turn on EFS lifecycle management to move cold files to Infrequent Access
Copy old files to an Amazon EBS volume with a nightly script
Switch the file system to provisioned throughput mode
Create a Lambda function that deletes files after 60 days
explanation: EFS lifecycle management automatically moves files that have not been accessed for a set number of days to the lower-cost Infrequent Access storage class. The files stay on the same file system and are read as before, with a small retrieval charge.

choiceExplanations.1: Copying files to EBS by script takes ongoing effort and moves the files off the shared file system.
choiceExplanations.2: Provisioned throughput changes how much throughput the file system has; it does not lower the cost of storing cold files.
choiceExplanations.3: Deleting files conflicts with the requirement that they stay on the file system.

question:
A company runs a steady workload on EC2 instances in us-east-1a for the next three years. It wants a discount, and it also needs capacity to be guaranteed in that Availability Zone when it launches instances.
Which purchasing option should it choose?
explanation: A zonal Reserved Instance gives a billing discount and also reserves capacity in a specific Availability Zone, which meets both requirements.

choiceExplanations.0: A regional Reserved Instance gives the discount and applies in any Availability Zone of the Region, but it does not reserve capacity.
choiceExplanations.1: Spot Instances are heavily discounted but can be interrupted, and capacity is not guaranteed.
choiceExplanations.3: On-Demand Instances carry no commitment and no discount, and capacity in a zone is not guaranteed.

question:
A pharmaceutical company stores clinical trial results in an Amazon S3 bucket in its data lake account (Account A). The objects are encrypted with SSE-KMS by using a customer managed key. A research partner that has its own AWS account (Account B) must read the objects from an IAM role in Account B. The security team requires least privilege, and it does not want the data copied or long-term credentials shared.
Which combination of actions will meet these requirements?
choices: Add a bucket policy in Account A that allows the role in Account B to read the objects, and re-encrypt the objects with the AWS managed key aws/s3 so that both accounts can decrypt them

Add a bucket policy in Account A that allows the role in Account B to read the objects, add a statement to the customer managed key's key policy that lets the role decrypt, and give the role s3:GetObject and kms:Decrypt permissions in Account B

Add a bucket policy in Account A that allows the role in Account B to read the objects, and give the role kms:Decrypt permission in Account B's IAM policy only, because KMS permissions can be granted entirely from the calling account

Add a statement to the customer managed key's key policy that lets the role in Account B decrypt, and give the role s3:GetObject permission in Account B's IAM policy, without any change to the bucket policy in Account A
explanation: Cross-account access to SSE-KMS objects needs both layers to allow it. S3 needs a bucket policy in the bucket owner's account plus matching IAM permissions in the other account, and KMS needs a key policy statement in the key's account plus IAM permission to use the key. This works only with a customer managed key.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS managed keys such as aws/s3 cannot be shared across accounts because their key policy cannot be changed, so the role in Account B could not decrypt the objects.
choiceExplanations.2: For a key in another account, the key policy must allow the other account's principal; an IAM policy in the calling account alone is not enough to use the key.
choiceExplanations.3: Without a bucket policy (or access point) in Account A that allows the role, the role has no permission to read objects in Account A's bucket, so an IAM policy in Account B is not enough.

resources.title: Allowing users in other accounts to use a KMS key

question:
A pharmaceutical company runs its clinical data platform on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance that was created without encryption. The CISO now requires that the database be encrypted at rest with AWS KMS, with as little data loss as possible. As the solutions architect, you review the approaches that the team proposes.
Which of the following approaches will NOT result in an encrypted database that contains the existing data?
choices: Take a snapshot, copy the snapshot with encryption enabled by using a KMS key, and restore the copy as a new DB instance
Create a new encrypted DB instance and use AWS Database Migration Service to replicate the data from the existing instance
Create a new encrypted DB instance and migrate the data with a native logical dump and restore by using pg_dump and pg_restore
Modify the existing DB instance, turn on encryption with a KMS key, and apply the change immediately
explanation: Encryption at rest can be set only when an RDS DB instance is created, so modifying an existing unencrypted instance cannot turn it on. The other approaches all end with an encrypted instance that holds the data: an encrypted copy of a snapshot restored as a new instance, a DMS migration, or a dump and restore into a new encrypted instance.

choiceExplanations.0: This is the standard path: a snapshot copy can be encrypted with a KMS key, and restoring that copy creates an encrypted instance with the existing data, so it does produce the required result.
choiceExplanations.1: DMS can replicate the data from the existing instance to a new encrypted instance, so this approach does produce an encrypted database holding the data.
choiceExplanations.2: A logical dump and restore into a new encrypted instance also results in an encrypted database that holds the data, so this approach is valid.

resources.title: Copying a DB snapshot for Amazon RDS

question:
A pharmaceutical company is building a mobile app that lets patients upload photos of their medication labels to a single Amazon S3 bucket. Patients sign in through an Amazon Cognito user pool. The security team requires that each patient can read and write only their own folder, named after the patient's identity, with no custom code to enforce it and the LEAST ongoing administration as patients are added.
Which solution meets these requirements?
choices: Use a Cognito identity pool whose authenticated role has an IAM policy that limits S3 access to the prefix built from the identity pool's identity ID policy variable
Create an IAM user for each patient with a policy that allows access to a folder named after the patient
Use the Cognito user pool ID token to call Amazon S3 directly, and add a bucket policy that matches the username in the token
Create one IAM role per patient and assign it through the identity pool's rule-based role mapping
explanation: A Cognito identity pool exchanges the user pool sign-in for temporary AWS credentials for an authenticated IAM role. Using the identity pool's identity ID policy variable in the role's S3 resource path limits each patient to their own prefix with a single policy and no per-patient administration.

choiceExplanations.1: Creating and managing an IAM user for every patient does not scale and relies on long-term credentials, the opposite of least ongoing administration.
choiceExplanations.2: S3 does not accept a Cognito user pool token as credentials; the token must be exchanged for AWS credentials through an identity pool.
choiceExplanations.3: A role for every patient means creating and maintaining roles as patients join, which is heavy administration; one role with a policy variable already isolates every patient.

resources.title: Amazon S3: Allows Amazon Cognito users to access objects in their bucket

question:
A pharmaceutical company is moving its drug-interaction API, packaged as Linux containers, to AWS. Traffic is unpredictable, and the API must stay available if an Availability Zone fails. The operations team is small and wants to avoid patching, scaling or capacity planning for servers. You are asked to recommend the design with the highest availability and the LEAST operational overhead.
Which solution should you recommend?
choices: Amazon ECS with the EC2 launch type, container instances in an Auto Scaling group across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer, and a capacity provider for scaling
Amazon EKS with self-managed nodes in an Auto Scaling group across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer
Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type, a service with tasks spread across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer, and service auto scaling on request count
Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type, a service with all tasks in one Availability Zone behind a Network Load Balancer
explanation: With the Fargate launch type, AWS runs the infrastructure for the tasks, so there are no instances to patch or scale. Spreading the service's tasks across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer keeps it available if a zone fails, and service auto scaling adjusts the task count to the traffic.

choiceExplanations.0: The EC2 launch type also spreads tasks across zones, but the team would still patch, scale and manage the container instances, which is more operational overhead than Fargate.
choiceExplanations.1: Self-managed EKS nodes carry the most operational work: node patching, scaling and Kubernetes version upgrades.
choiceExplanations.3: Running all tasks in one Availability Zone fails the requirement that the API stays available if a zone fails.

resources.title: Architect for AWS Fargate for Amazon ECS
Automatically scale your Amazon ECS service

question:
A pharmaceutical company hosts a clinical portal behind an internal Application Load Balancer in each of two Regions. The load balancers are in private subnets and are reached through a private hosted zone from the company's VPCs, which are connected across Regions. The networking team needs Route 53 to fail over to the secondary Region automatically when the primary application becomes unhealthy.
Which TWO steps should you take? (Choose TWO.)
choices: Create a Route 53 health check that sends HTTPS requests to the internal load balancer's DNS name
Create a CloudWatch alarm on the primary load balancer's unhealthy host count metric
Create a Route 53 health check that monitors the CloudWatch alarm, and associate it with the primary failover record
Move the internal load balancers into public subnets so that the Route 53 health checkers can reach them
Create weighted records with a weight of zero for the secondary Region, and raise the weight manually during an incident
explanation: Route 53 health checkers run outside your VPC and cannot reach private endpoints. For private resources, create a CloudWatch alarm on a metric that reflects the application's health, and a Route 53 health check that monitors the alarm; associate that health check with the primary failover record.

choiceExplanations.0: The Route 53 health checkers are outside the VPC and cannot reach an internal load balancer, so this health check would always report unhealthy.
choiceExplanations.3: Making the load balancers public exposes the portal and contradicts the internal design; the alarm-based health check solves the problem without changing the architecture.
choiceExplanations.4: Changing weights by hand is not automatic failover; it depends on a person noticing the incident.

resources.title: Configuring failover in a private hosted zone
Types of Amazon Route 53 health checks

question:
A pharmaceutical company runs its research platform on an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster with one writer and five Aurora Replicas. Two of the replicas use a larger instance class (db.r5.2xlarge) than the other three (db.r5.large). Data scientists run long analytical queries that must run only on the two larger replicas, and the application's normal read traffic must not reach those two. The company wants the LEAST application configuration to maintain.
Which solution meets these requirements?
choices: Have the data scientists connect to the reader endpoint, and have the application connect to the writer endpoint so that its reads never reach the replicas
Create one custom endpoint that contains the two larger replicas for the data scientists, and keep the application on the reader endpoint, which balances connections across the replicas
Create a second Aurora cluster with larger instances by using Aurora cloning, point the data scientists to the clone's reader endpoint, and keep the application on the original cluster
Create one custom endpoint that contains the two larger replicas for the data scientists, and another custom endpoint that contains the three smaller replicas for the application's reads
explanation: Custom endpoints let you define a subset of Aurora Replicas. The reader endpoint always balances connections across all replicas, so keeping application reads off the larger instances needs a second custom endpoint that contains only the smaller replicas.

choiceExplanations.0: The reader endpoint spreads connections across all five replicas, so analytical and normal reads would share every replica, and sending the application to the writer endpoint moves its reads onto the writer.
choiceExplanations.1: The reader endpoint still includes the two larger replicas, so the application's read traffic would reach them and compete with the analytical queries.
choiceExplanations.2: A clone is a separate cluster created as a point-in-time copy; it adds cost and does not stay in sync, and the requirements can be met with endpoints alone.

question:
A pharmaceutical company runs an online training game for its sales representatives. The game shows a real-time leaderboard ranked by score and updated thousands of times per second. The leaderboard runs on a single cache node, and a node failure last month wiped it out and caused an outage. As the solutions architect, you must make the leaderboard highly available with sub-millisecond reads and the LEAST change to the ranking logic.
Which solution should you choose?
choices: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with several nodes in different Availability Zones, with the leaderboard data sharded across the nodes
Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with a primary node and replicas in different Availability Zones, with Multi-AZ and automatic failover enabled
Amazon ElastiCache for Redis as a single large node, with daily backups of the cache to Amazon S3 for recovery
Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the table, using the score as the sort key to rank the players
explanation: Redis supports sorted sets, which keep elements ranked by score, so the ranking logic can stay as it is. A replication group with replicas in other Availability Zones and Multi-AZ automatic failover promotes a replica if the primary fails, so the leaderboard survives a node failure.

choiceExplanations.0: Memcached has no replication or high availability: its nodes shard the data, so losing a node loses that part of the cache, and it has no sorted-set data type.
choiceExplanations.2: A single node is still a single point of failure; backups help you restore after an outage but give no automatic failover.
choiceExplanations.3: DynamoDB with DAX has no sorted-set operation, so ranking would need different data modeling and queries, and DAX caches reads rather than maintaining rankings.

resources.title: Common ElastiCache Use Cases and How ElastiCache Can Help
Minimizing downtime in ElastiCache by using Multi-AZ with Valkey and Redis OSS

question:
A pharmaceutical company streams lab instrument telemetry over TCP to an application behind a Network Load Balancer. The load balancer has the same number of targets in each of three Availability Zones, and cross-zone load balancing is turned on. The finance team has noticed large data transfer charges between Availability Zones, and the company must keep the application deployed across all three zones. You are asked to reduce the cost.
Which action should you take?
choices: Move all targets into one Availability Zone and keep the Network Load Balancer
Replace the Network Load Balancer with an Application Load Balancer
Turn off cross-zone load balancing on the Network Load Balancer and keep the same number of targets in each Availability Zone
Keep cross-zone load balancing on and register the targets by IP address instead of by instance ID
explanation: With cross-zone load balancing on, each Network Load Balancer node sends traffic to targets in every enabled zone, and traffic that crosses zones is billed as data transfer between Availability Zones. Turning it off keeps each node's traffic inside its own zone. Because every zone has the same number of targets, the load stays even and the deployment remains across three zones.

choiceExplanations.0: Moving all targets into one zone removes the multi-zone deployment, which the company must keep.
choiceExplanations.1: An Application Load Balancer works at the HTTP and HTTPS layer and cannot carry raw TCP telemetry, so changing the type would break the application.
choiceExplanations.3: Registering targets by IP address changes how targets are registered, not whether traffic crosses zones, so the inter-zone charges remain.

resources.title: Edit target group attributes for your Network Load Balancer
Edit attributes for your Network Load Balancer

question:
A pharmaceutical company runs nightly genomic sequencing jobs that restart from checkpoints, so Spot interruptions are acceptable. The jobs need 400 vCPUs and can run on several instance types in any of three Availability Zones. You are asked to launch the capacity with a Spot Fleet at the lowest cost while keeping the number of interruptions low.
Which configuration should you choose?
choices: A Spot Fleet with the lowestPrice allocation strategy and a single instance type in one Availability Zone
A Spot Fleet with the capacityOptimized allocation strategy and several instance types in all three Availability Zones
A Spot Fleet with the priceCapacityOptimized allocation strategy and several instance types in all three Availability Zones
A Spot Fleet with the diversified allocation strategy and several instance types in all three Availability Zones
explanation: The priceCapacityOptimized strategy picks the pools with the highest available capacity, which have the lowest chance of interruption, and then chooses the lowest-priced among them, so it balances low cost against few interruptions. Offering several instance types across three zones gives it many pools to choose from.

choiceExplanations.0: lowestPrice selects the cheapest pool without regard to capacity, and a single instance type in one zone offers only one pool, so interruptions are more likely.
choiceExplanations.1: capacityOptimized favors the pools with the most capacity to reduce interruptions, but it does not optimize for price, so it may not give the lowest cost.
choiceExplanations.3: diversified spreads capacity across all pools to improve availability for long workloads, but it does not choose pools by price or by available capacity.

resources.title: Use allocation strategies to determine how EC2 Fleet or Spot Fleet fulfills Spot and On-Demand capacity

question: Which AWS service places compute and storage at the edge of telecom carrier networks for low-latency mobile apps?
explanation: AWS Wavelength deploys standard AWS compute and storage services at the edge of communications service providers' networks, so applications can reach mobile devices and end users with very low latency.

choiceExplanations.1: AWS Outposts is AWS-managed infrastructure that runs in your own data center or co-location facility, not at the edge of a carrier's network.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon CloudFront delivers web content to users from edge locations; it is a content delivery network, not a place to run your own application servers inside carrier networks.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Direct Connect links your internal network to AWS over a dedicated fiber connection; it does not host compute or storage.

question: When is AWS Wavelength the best choice?
choices: To run apps inside carrier networks
To link a data center to AWS
To run AWS hardware in your data center
explanation: Wavelength Zones sit in communications service providers' locations, so you run latency-sensitive applications on resources such as EC2 instances there while they stay connected to the parent AWS Region.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon CloudFront caches and delivers static and dynamic web content from edge locations; it does not run your application inside a carrier's network.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Direct Connect links your internal network to AWS over a dedicated fiber connection; it does not run applications at the carrier edge.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Outposts runs AWS-managed infrastructure in your own data center or co-location facility, which is a different place from a carrier's network edge.

question: Which AWS service lets you find, share and deploy prebuilt serverless applications, including ones from the community?
explanation: The AWS Serverless Application Repository lets developers and organizations find, deploy and publish serverless applications, sharing them publicly with the community or privately within a team or organization.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS Lambda runs your code without servers to manage, but it is the compute service, not a place to browse and share prebuilt applications.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon ECR is a managed registry for container images, not for serverless applications.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Elastic Beanstalk deploys web applications that you build and provisions the infrastructure for them; it is not a catalog of prebuilt serverless applications.

resources.title: What Is the AWS Serverless Application Repository?

question: When would you use the AWS Serverless Application Repository?
choices: To store and share container images
To run functions triggered by events
explanation: You use it to browse applications that other developers have published and deploy one with a few clicks, or to publish your own serverless application for others to use.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon ECR is the managed registry for storing and managing container images.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS Lambda runs your code in response to events or API calls; it is the engine that runs functions, not the place to find prebuilt applications.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Config provides a detailed view of how your resources are configured and how those configurations change over time.

resources.title: What Is the AWS Serverless Application Repository?

question: Which AWS offering lets you register on-premises servers to an Amazon ECS cluster and run container tasks on them?
explanation: Amazon ECS Anywhere lets you register an external instance, such as an on-premises server or virtual machine, to your Amazon ECS cluster and run tasks on it with the EXTERNAL launch type.

choiceExplanations.1: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling keeps the right number of EC2 instances running in AWS for your load; it does not add your own servers to an ECS cluster.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Fargate runs containers without servers to manage, but on AWS-managed capacity, not on your own on-premises servers.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Elastic Beanstalk deploys web applications into the AWS Cloud and provisions EC2 instances or EKS clusters for them; it does not turn your on-premises servers into ECS capacity.

resources.title: Amazon ECS clusters for external instances

question: When should you choose Amazon ECS Anywhere?
explanation: ECS Anywhere is built for running container workloads on your own on-premises servers or virtual machines, which Amazon ECS manages as external instances in a cluster.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon ElastiCache sets up, manages and scales a distributed in-memory data store or cache.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon SQS is a hosted queue that lets you integrate and decouple distributed software systems and components.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon ECR is a managed container image registry for pushing, pulling and managing images.

resources.title: Amazon ECS clusters for external instances

question: Which AWS offering lets you create and operate Kubernetes clusters on your own infrastructure, even in air-gapped sites?
explanation: Amazon EKS Anywhere is a customer-managed product that simplifies Kubernetes cluster management in on-premises and edge environments, and it can run in air-gapped environments.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon ECS Anywhere extends Amazon ECS, which is the AWS container service that is not Kubernetes, to external servers.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS Fargate runs containers on AWS-managed capacity without servers to manage; it does not run on your own on-premises infrastructure.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Lambda runs your code in response to events without servers to manage; it is not a way to run Kubernetes clusters on your own infrastructure.

resources.title: Deploy Amazon EKS clusters across cloud and on-premises environments

question: What is Amazon EKS Anywhere mainly used for?
choices: To store and share container images
To run code in response to events
explanation: EKS Anywhere is for running Kubernetes clusters in your own on-premises or edge environments. It simplifies infrastructure setup and cluster lifecycle operations, but you stay responsible for maintaining the clusters.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS Fargate runs containers without servers or clusters of EC2 instances to manage, on AWS-managed capacity.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon ECR is the managed registry where you push, pull and manage container images.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Lambda runs code in response to events or API calls without servers to manage.

resources.title: Deploy Amazon EKS clusters across cloud and on-premises environments

question: Which AWS offering is the AWS distribution of the Kubernetes components behind Amazon EKS, usable with your own tooling?
explanation: Amazon EKS Distro is the AWS distribution of the underlying Kubernetes components that power all Amazon EKS offerings, and you can use it to self-manage Kubernetes clusters with your choice of tooling.

choiceExplanations.1: AWS Elastic Beanstalk deploys web applications and provisions the infrastructure for them; it does not provide Kubernetes components for you to run yourself.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Fargate runs containers without servers to manage; it is not a distribution of Kubernetes components.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon ECS Anywhere registers external servers to an Amazon ECS cluster; ECS is the AWS container service that is not Kubernetes.

resources.title: Deploy Amazon EKS clusters across cloud and on-premises environments

question: What job is Amazon EKS Distro built for?
choices: To store and share container images
explanation: EKS Distro gives you the Kubernetes components that power Amazon EKS so that you can self-manage Kubernetes clusters with your own tooling. Such deployments are not covered by AWS Support Plans.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS Fargate runs containers without servers or clusters of EC2 instances to manage, on AWS-managed capacity.
choiceExplanations.2: Elastic Load Balancing automatically distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances, containers and IP addresses.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon ECR is the managed registry where you push, pull and manage container images.

resources.title: Deploy Amazon EKS clusters across cloud and on-premises environments

question: Which AWS database service lets you run existing Apache Cassandra workloads without managing any servers?
explanation: Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) is a serverless, managed, Cassandra-compatible database, so you can run existing Cassandra workloads with the same application code and developer tools.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon DocumentDB is a managed database that is compatible with MongoDB, not with Apache Cassandra.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon Neptune is a managed graph database for highly connected datasets.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon ElastiCache sets up and scales a distributed in-memory data store or cache, not a Cassandra database.

resources.title: What is Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra)?

question: What need is Amazon Keyspaces the best fit for?
choices: To cache hot data in memory
To query highly connected graph data
explanation: Keyspaces makes it easy to migrate, run and scale Apache Cassandra workloads in AWS without deploying infrastructure or installing software.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon ElastiCache provides a distributed in-memory data store or cache.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon Neptune is the graph database for building applications that work with highly connected datasets.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon DocumentDB is the managed database that is compatible with MongoDB.

resources.title: What is Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra)?

question: Which service lets remote users securely reach VPC and on-premises resources through an OpenVPN-based client?
explanation: AWS Client VPN is a managed, client-based VPN service that lets users securely access AWS and on-premises resources from any location using an OpenVPN-based client.

choiceExplanations.1: AWS Site-to-Site VPN connects your VPC to your own on-premises network or remote device, not the individual computers of remote users.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Direct Connect links your internal network to AWS over a dedicated fiber connection; it is not a VPN client service for individual users.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS PrivateLink privately connects your VPC to services and resources as if they were in your VPC; it does not give remote users VPN access.

question: What task is AWS Client VPN designed for?
choices: To connect a branch office network
To give remote users VPN access
To filter traffic in a VPC
explanation: Client VPN is meant for individual people who work from any location and need secure access to AWS and on-premises resources through an OpenVPN-based VPN client.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates a connection between your VPC and your own on-premises network, which suits linking a whole site rather than individual users.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Network Firewall filters traffic at the perimeter of your VPC.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS PrivateLink privately connects your VPC to services and resources, and lets you make your own endpoint service available to other customers.

question: Which AWS security service continually scans EC2 instances, ECR container images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities?
explanation: Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability management service that discovers workloads and continually scans EC2 instances, container images in Amazon ECR and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that analyzes logs and other AWS data sources for suspicious activity; it does not scan your workloads for software vulnerabilities.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in Amazon S3 using machine learning and pattern matching.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Config records how your resources are configured and how those configurations change over time.

question: When should you choose Amazon Inspector?
choices: To discover sensitive data in S3
explanation: Use Inspector to find software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure in your EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions; it creates a finding for each issue it detects.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon Macie is the service that discovers sensitive data in Amazon S3.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon Detective helps you analyze, investigate and identify the root cause of security findings or suspicious activities.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Artifact provides on-demand downloads of AWS security and compliance documents.

question: Which AWS security service automatically finds sensitive data, such as personal information, stored in Amazon S3 buckets?
explanation: Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in Amazon S3 using machine learning and pattern matching, and it generates a finding when it detects such data in an object.

choiceExplanations.1: Amazon Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure, not for sensitive data in S3.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS KMS creates and controls the keys used to encrypt and sign data; it does not search your buckets for sensitive data.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Secrets Manager manages, retrieves and rotates credentials and other secrets; it does not scan your S3 data.

question: What task does Amazon Macie help you with?
choices: To encrypt data with managed keys
To find personal data in S3
explanation: Macie detects sensitive data, such as personal information, in S3 objects and gives you findings to review and remediate. It also evaluates the security and access control of your S3 buckets.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS KMS is the service that creates and controls the keys used to encrypt data.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon Inspector is the service that scans EC2 instances and other workloads for software vulnerabilities.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS WAF monitors the HTTP(S) requests sent to your web application resources and controls access to your content.

question: Which AWS security service helps you find the root cause of security findings using machine learning, graph theory and visualizations?
explanation: Amazon Detective collects log data from your AWS resources and uses machine learning, statistical analysis and graph theory to build visualizations that help you investigate the root cause of security findings.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon GuardDuty is the threat detection service that produces findings about suspicious activity; Detective is the service you use to investigate such findings.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS Config records how your resources are configured and how they change over time; it does not investigate security findings.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Shield protects internet-facing applications against distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks; it does not investigate security findings.

question: What would you use Amazon Detective for?
choices: To record API calls in an account
explanation: Detective helps you analyze and investigate suspicious activity and quickly identify the root cause of security findings.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS CloudTrail records the actions taken by users, roles and AWS services in your account as events.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon Inspector is the service that scans workloads for software vulnerabilities.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS WAF lets you monitor and control the HTTP(S) requests sent to your protected web application resources.

question: Which service gives you on-demand downloads of AWS security and compliance reports, such as SOC and ISO?
explanation: AWS Artifact provides on-demand downloads of AWS security and compliance documents, such as ISO and PCI reports and SOC reports, free of charge.

choiceExplanations.1: AWS Config shows how your own resources are configured and how that changes over time; it does not provide AWS's compliance reports.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS CloudTrail records the actions taken in your account as events; it is not a source of AWS compliance reports.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS KMS creates and controls the keys used to encrypt and sign your data; it does not provide compliance reports.

question: Why would you use AWS Artifact?
choices: To log API activity in an account
To create and manage encryption keys
explanation: Use Artifact when an auditor or regulator needs evidence of AWS's security and compliance: you download the reports and certifications and can submit them as audit artifacts.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS Config gives a detailed view of your resource configurations and how they change over time.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS CloudTrail records the actions taken by users, roles and AWS services in your account as events.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS KMS is the service that creates and controls the keys used to encrypt and sign data.

question: Which service lets you create a resource once and share it with other AWS accounts or your organization?
explanation: AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) lets you create a resource once and share it with other accounts, or with accounts in your organization or OUs, so you do not duplicate the resource in every account.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS Organizations creates, groups and governs accounts and simplifies billing; sharing a resource across those accounts is what AWS RAM does.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS IAM Identity Center connects your workforce users to AWS applications and accounts; it does not share resources between accounts.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Control Tower sets up and governs a multi-account environment using prescriptive best practices and guardrails; it is not the service for sharing resources.

resources.title: What is AWS Resource Access Manager?

question: When would you use AWS RAM?
choices: To connect workforce users to AWS
To set up accounts with guardrails
To group accounts under one bill
explanation: Use AWS RAM when several accounts need the same resource: you create it once and share it, which reduces duplicate resources and keeps a single set of policies and permissions for them.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS IAM Identity Center is the AWS solution for connecting your workforce users to AWS applications and accounts.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS Control Tower sets up and governs a multi-account environment and applies guardrails to it.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Organizations lets you group accounts and simplify billing with a single payment method for all of them.

resources.title: What is AWS Resource Access Manager?

question: Which AWS service can transcribe recorded calls, convert live speech to text and redact personal data?
explanation: Amazon Transcribe is an automatic speech recognition service that converts audio to text, either as a live stream or from files in Amazon S3, and it can redact personally identifiable information.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon Polly does the reverse job: it converts text into lifelike speech.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and videos to detect objects, text and faces; it does not transcribe speech.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon Translate converts text from one language to another; it does not turn audio into text.

question: When would you use Amazon Translate?
choices: To turn written text into spoken audio
To convert recorded speech into text
To detect the sentiment of a review
explanation: Amazon Translate is a text translation service that uses machine learning to translate text documents and application content from one language to another.

choiceExplanations.1: Turning written text into spoken audio is the job of Amazon Polly.
choiceExplanations.2: Converting recorded speech into text is what Amazon Transcribe does.
choiceExplanations.3: Detecting the sentiment of text is a job for Amazon Comprehend.

question: Which AWS service can extract typed text, handwriting, forms and tables from scanned documents?
explanation: Amazon Textract detects typed and handwritten text and extracts forms and tables from documents such as scans, images and PDFs.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon Comprehend finds insights such as entities, key phrases and sentiment in text, rather than extracting forms and tables from scans.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon Transcribe converts spoken audio to text; it does not read documents.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon Polly converts text into lifelike speech; it does not read documents.

question: When would you use Amazon Comprehend?
choices: To read text from scanned forms
To build voice and text chatbots
explanation: Amazon Comprehend uses natural language processing to extract insights from text, such as entities, key phrases, language and sentiment.

choiceExplanations.0: Reading text from scanned forms is what Amazon Textract does.
choiceExplanations.1: Building voice and text chatbots is the job of Amazon Lex.
choiceExplanations.3: Turning speech into text is what Amazon Transcribe does.

question: Which AWS service can build chatbots that take voice or text input and understand what the user wants?
explanation: Amazon Lex builds conversational interfaces for voice and text, using automatic speech recognition and natural language understanding to work out the intent behind what the user says or types.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon Polly converts text into speech; it does not interpret a user's request.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon Textract extracts text and data from documents rather than holding conversations.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and videos; it does not build chatbots.

question: When would you use Amazon SageMaker AI?
choices: To build and train ML models
To read text from scanned forms
To turn text into lifelike speech
explanation: Amazon SageMaker AI is a fully managed machine learning service that lets data scientists and developers build, train and deploy ML models.
